waterbodySystem: Imus–Ylang Ylang–Rio Grande Rivers (IYRR) basin-management system; do not merge its three named rivers into a single fish-occurrence locality
question: Do the public IRBM/SORB outputs supply fish species evidence or a retrievable final report for the separate CvSU Imus River watershed biophysical-characterization project?

sourceReviews.title: Bio-physical Characterization, Vulnerability and Pollution Assessment in Imus River Watershed
sourceReviews.finding: CvSU’s official Research Center listing identifies the project under Prof. Noel A. Sedigo, CAFENR, PEMSEA, and the period November 2020-April 2021. The listing does not provide its report, fish methods, sampling sites, taxa, or data. This remains a distinct bibliographic lead; it is not established as the SORB or complete ASEANO mapping output.

sourceReviews.title: IRBM Stories: Restoring the Flow — Imus–Ylang Ylang–Rio Grande Rivers
sourceReviews.finding: The public management profile cites the IYRR SORB Report 2025 for selected basin statistics and includes a historical river-ranger recollection of fish abundance, but it contains no named fish taxa in the reviewed text. A targeted search for “species” in the PDF found no match. The profile does not expose the full SORB report. Its catchment map and reported environmental facts are not fish records, fishing-area geometry, or current safety evidence.

sourceReviews.title: Mid-Term Progress Review of the Sustainable Development Strategy for the Seas of East Asia Implementation Plan — SORB progress excerpt
sourceReviews.finding: The official PEMSEA mid-term progress excerpt says that, as of June 2025, four SORB reports—including IYRR—had been developed and were undergoing final review. This is dated project-status evidence, not confirmation that the IYRR report was finalized or publicly released by November 2026.

sourceReviews.title: 2025 Annual FASPs Portfolio Report — IRBM Project section
sourceReviews.finding: The downloaded official 170-page annual report was text-checked on pages 50 and 111. It says the IYRR/Pasac-Guagua SORB reports were drafted and validation workshops conducted; it separately says the WEFE analysis report was finalized. This high-level project summary does not supply or characterize the underlying SORB as a fish inventory and does not establish that it lacks fish information.

retrieval.outcome: The searches located an official public IYRR management profile, the DENR annual portfolio report, and time-bounded SORB development status. No direct downloadable full IYRR SORB report or the distinct CvSU project deliverable was located in the reviewed results. This is a bounded retrieval outcome, not proof that the reports or fish data do not exist or are unavailable elsewhere.
limitations: The PEMSEA site profile is a secondary public summary and cites an underlying IYRR SORB Report 2025 without linking its full text in the reviewed page.
The June 2025 mid-term status and 2025 annual portfolio wording describe draft/final-review stages; they do not establish a later release or final status in 2026.
The targeted “species” text search is limited to the public profile PDF and cannot establish the content of the unreviewed full SORB report.
The CvSU Research Center listing is bibliographic metadata only; its titled report and any fish-specific tables remain unreviewed.
IYRR basin-level maps and measurements do not constitute a reusable river-channel, municipal-water, or fishing-ground geometry.

environmentalContext.fecalColiform: The PEMSEA public profile attributes a midstream figure of 16,000,000 MPN/100 mL to the IYRR SORB Report 2025 but the reviewed passage exposes no sample date, station-level dataset, or methodology. It is historical/secondary context only and must not be used as a current safety warning.
environmentalContext.basinDimensions: The profile attributes aggregate area and river-network figures to the IRBM Project Document/SORB. These are retained only as source-reported context, not as vector geometry or an adopted fishing area.
environmentalContext.separation: Environmental conditions and basin management status are separate from fish presence, water safety, legal access, catchability, and diet.

rightsReview.decision: Keep only minimal attributed bibliography, report-status chronology, and retrieval notes. Do not republish report text, maps, measurements, or datasets without item-specific review.
